1.translation: Arjuna said: I wish to know Nature, the Person, the field, the knower of the field, knowledge, and the object of knowledge, O Keśava.

2.translation: The Blessed Lord said: This body is called the field, O son of Kuntī; one who knows this is called the knower of the field by those who know this subject. Śrīdhara explains “field” as the body, the ground from which worldly existence sprouts, and “knower” as the one who regards it as “I” and “mine” and experiences its results.

3.translation: Know Me also as the knower of the field in all fields, O Bhārata. The knowledge of the field and the knower of the field—that is what I regard as knowledge. Śrīdhara says that other learning, when it does not produce this discrimination, is merely empty scholarship because it remains a cause of bondage.
word_for_word: of the field and the knower of the field

4.translation: Hear briefly from Me what that field is, of what nature it is, what its changes are, from what it arises, and who the knower is and what his power is.

5.translation: This field and its subject have been sung in many ways by sages, separately in various Vedic meters, and also in the reasoned and decisive statements of the Brahma-sūtras. Śrīdhara includes both the Upaniṣadic sentences that establish Brahman’s characteristics and the aphorisms that establish it through reasoning.
word_for_word: by Vedic meters or the Vedas
by the statements or aphorisms of the Brahma-sūtras

6.translation: The five great elements, ego, intellect, the Unmanifest, the ten senses, the one mind, and the five objects of the senses.

7.translation: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the bodily aggregate, consciousness, and steadfastness—this field, together with its modifications, has been described in brief. Śrīdhara notes that desire and the like are observable and therefore belong to the mind within the field, not to the Self.

8.translation: Humility, absence of pretence, nonviolence, forbearance, straightforwardness, service to the teacher, purity, steadfastness, and self-control.

9.translation: Dispassion toward the objects of the senses, absence of ego, and repeatedly seeing the defect and suffering in birth, death, old age, and disease.
word_for_word: toward the objects of the senses
birth, death, old age, and disease
seeing repeatedly the defect and suffering

10.translation: Nonattachment, absence of excessive identification with son, wife, and home, and constant even-mindedness in the attainment of what is desired and undesired.
word_for_word: absence of excessive identification or clinging
toward son, wife, home, and the like
in the arrival of desired and undesired things

11.translation: Undivided, unwavering devotion to Me through exclusive Yoga, residence in a secluded place, and absence of delight in the assemblies of ordinary people.

12.translation: Constancy in spiritual knowledge and seeing the purpose of knowledge of Reality. This is declared to be knowledge; what is contrary to this is declared to be ignorance, and is to be abandoned. Śrīdhara explains that the purpose of true knowledge is liberation.
word_for_word: seeing the purpose of knowledge of Reality

13.translation: I will declare what is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality: the beginningless, supreme Brahman, said to be neither being nor non-being. Śrīdhara explains that it lies beyond both the manifest object of affirmative knowledge and the unmanifest object of negation.

14.translation: It has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and mouths everywhere; it has ears everywhere, pervades everything in the world, and stands after enveloping all.
word_for_word: having eyes, heads, and mouths everywhere

15.translation: It appears through the qualities of all the senses, yet is free from all the senses; unattached, it supports all; without the guṇas, it is also the experiencer and sustainer of the guṇas.
word_for_word: appearing through the qualities of all the senses
the experiencer or sustainer of the guṇas

16.translation: It is outside and inside beings, the moving and the unmoving; because of its subtlety it is unknowable, and it is both far away and near. Śrīdhara explains that it is far for the ignorant, as though separated by immense distance, but ever near as the inner Self for the wise.

17.translation: It is undivided among beings, yet appears to stand as though divided; it is to be known as the sustainer of beings, the devourer at dissolution, and the originator at creation.
word_for_word: the originator, one who brings forth

18.translation: It is the light of lights, said to be beyond darkness; it is knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the goal reached through knowledge, seated in the heart of everyone. Śrīdhara explains that this light illumines even the sun and moon and is revealed in the movement of understanding.

19.translation: Thus the field, knowledge, and what is to be known have been stated briefly. My devotee, understanding this, becomes fit for My nature—that is, for Brahman.

20.translation: Know both Nature and the Person to be beginningless; know the modifications and the guṇas also to arise from Nature. Śrīdhara explains Nature as the beginningless power of the Lord and the Person as beginningless because he is a portion of Him.

21.translation: Nature is said to be the cause in the agency of the body and senses; the Person is said to be the cause in the experiencing of pleasure and pain. Śrīdhara explains that Nature’s agency and the Person’s experiencing are spoken of because of their association, although Nature is insentient and the Person is unchanging.

22.translation: The Person, abiding in Nature, indeed experiences the guṇas born of Nature; attachment to the guṇas is the cause of his births in good and bad wombs. Śrīdhara explains that the Person seems to experience because he identifies with the body produced by Nature.
word_for_word: in births in good and bad wombs

23.translation: The Person within this body is said to be the witness, the consenter, the supporter, the experiencer, the great Lord, and the Supreme Self—the transcendent Person. Śrīdhara explains the witness as standing apart, the consenter as helping by mere presence, and the supporter as the inner ruler.
word_for_word: the witness, standing near and apart

24.translation: One who thus knows the Person and Nature together with the guṇas, however he may live, is not born again. He is liberated.
word_for_word: even while living in any manner
that one is not born again

25.translation: Some see the Self in the self through meditation; others through Sāṅkhya, by examining the difference between Nature and the Person; and others through Yoga or through Karma Yoga. Śrīdhara presents these as alternative emphases according to the practitioner’s discipline, even though the practices may be combined in sequence.

26.translation: Others, not knowing this in such a way, hear from others—the teachers—and worship or meditate; they too, devoted to what they hear, certainly cross over mortality and worldly existence.

27.translation: Whatever being comes into existence—moving or unmoving—know that all of it arises from the conjunction of the field and the knower of the field, O best of the Bharatas. Śrīdhara explains this conjunction as identification and superimposition, not a literal fusion of the two.
word_for_word: from the conjunction of field and knower of the field

28.translation: One who sees the Supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings, the Imperishable within the perishing, truly sees.

29.translation: For seeing the Lord equally present everywhere, one does not injure the Self by the self; therefore one reaches the supreme goal. Śrīdhara explains that denying the Self through ignorance is self-destruction, whereas this vision leads to liberation.

30.translation: One who sees that actions are performed in every way by Nature alone, and likewise sees the Self as non-doer, truly sees. Śrīdhara emphasizes that the Self’s agency arises only from identification with the body, not from its own nature.

31.translation: When one sees the distinctness of beings as resting in the One, and their expansion arising from that very One, then one becomes Brahman. Śrīdhara explains that recognizing all beings as no more than Nature’s forms removes the appearance of separateness.

32.translation: Because it is beginningless and without guṇas, this Supreme Self is imperishable. Though abiding in the body, O son of Kuntī, it neither acts nor is tainted.

33.translation: Just as all-pervading space, because of its subtlety, is not tainted, so the Self, abiding everywhere in bodies, is not tainted.

34.translation: Just as one sun illumines this entire world, so the knower of the field illumines the entire field, O Bhārata.

35.translation: Those who know, through the eye of knowledge, this distinction between the field and the knower of the field, and the liberation of beings from Nature, reach the Supreme.
word_for_word: of the field and the knower of the field
the liberation of beings from Nature
